poc_summary: Crafted a 120-byte Sony Wave64 (W64) file (/poc/poc2.w64) with a 'fmt ' chunk declaring codec tag 0x0045 (ADPCM_G726), channels=9, sample_rate=1, nAvgBytesPerSec=0x10000000, block_align=1, bits_per_coded_sample=4, plus a minimal 'data' chunk so header parsing completes. In ff_get_wav_header the G.726 special-case sets bits_per_coded_sample = bit_rate/sample_rate = 2147483648, which truncates to INT32_MIN (-2147483648) when stored in the 32-bit field. w64_read_header's block_align sanity check then computes ((bits_per_coded_sample+7)/8) * nb_channels = -268435455 * 9, which overflows a 32-bit int (signed integer overflow UB), wrapping to 1879048201 and corrupting st->codecpar->block_align. A small harness program (/poc/poc.c, run via run_poc's command on every version) opens the PoC via avformat_open_input, linked against each revision's own built libavformat.a/libavcodec.a/libswresample.a/libavutil.a, and prints codecpar->block_align/channels/bits_per_coded_sample/bit_rate.
explanation: Verified via reproduction using run_poc identically on all three configured versions (pre_intro, post_intro, post_benign) with the same PoC file (/poc/poc2.w64) and the same harness-build-and-run command. The W64 PoC (channels=9, sample_rate=1, codec tag 0x0045/ADPCM_G726, nAvgBytesPerSec=0x10000000) drives bits_per_coded_sample to INT32_MIN via the pre-existing G.726 bit_rate/sample_rate override, then exercises w64_read_header's block_align sanity check (the code added by the intro commit). Results: pre_intro -> block_align=1 (the check doesn't exist yet in this revision, so the raw fmt-chunk value passes through unmodified); post_intro -> block_align=1879048201 (the 32-bit signed multiplication -268435455*9 overflows int range and wraps -- this is the exact UB class OSS-Fuzz's UBSan flagged, 'signed integer overflow: ... cannot be represented in type int', in the same w64_read_header block_align expression); post_benign -> block_align=1 again, matching pre_intro, because the fix widens the intermediate to int64_t, removing the UB. This clean 3-way divergence (unaffected -> corrupted -> restored), combined with the source diff exactly matching meta.json's root-cause description and the intro/fix commits' actual code changes, confirms intro_verified=yes and benign_verified=yes. The sandbox's ASan-only build cannot trap the UB itself (no UBSan configured in this build), so a behavioral oracle (the corrupted vs. correct block_align value, an unambiguous, deterministic, target-exercised observation) was used instead of a raw sanitizer trap, consistent with the guidance for cases where the labelled UB doesn't crash under the available sanitizer instrumentation.

oracle.description: Print the demuxed AVCodecParameters.block_align after avformat_open_input() on the W64 PoC, run via run_poc with the identical command and input file on pre_intro, post_intro, and post_benign. Pre-fix/unaffected builds must report block_align=1 (the original fmt-chunk value, unmodified because either the sanity-check code does not exist yet, or it is computed without overflow). The introduced-bug build must report a corrupted, wrapped block_align (1879048201) produced by the 32-bit signed multiplication overflow.
oracle.target_evidence: Source diff confirms the mechanism: pre_intro (84e0e2f43e42) has no block_align sanity-check in w64_read_header's 'fmt ' handling at all. post_intro (71716406e68a) adds: `int block_align = st->codecpar->block_align; block_align = FFMAX(block_align, ((st->codecpar->bits_per_coded_sample + 7) / 8) * st->codecpar->ch_layout.nb_channels);` using plain 32-bit `int` arithmetic -- exactly the root cause described in meta.json, and exactly what OSS-Fuzz's UBSan report ("signed integer overflow: -251517880 * 32 cannot be represented in type 'int'") caught in this same function/expression. post_benign (fix 1afbc4087506) changes the intermediate to `int64_t block_align` and computes `((bits_per_coded_sample + 7LL) / 8) * nb_channels`, eliminating the overflow. Confirmed by reading source in each built container. The sandbox's sanitizer build here is ASan-only (no UBSan instrumentation, verified via configure flags: only -fsanitize=address), so the UB does not trap/crash under this harness's build config; instead it silently wraps at -O1, which is directly observable and reproducible as a corrupted block_align value gated by the exact intro/fix diff, giving a reliable behavioral oracle for the same labelled IntegerOverflow bug. Confirmed reproducible identically via both docker_shell and run_poc.
